identity.title: An ALMA Dynamical Mass Estimate of the Proposed Planetary-mass Companion FW Tau C

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) 1.3 mm observations of FW Tau C, a proposed $\sim$10 $M_{\rm Jup}$ planet-mass companion

targets.name: FW Tau C (companion to FW Tau AB)

question.value: Is FW Tau C a ~10 Mjup planetary-mass companion or a low-mass star? Measured via Keplerian rotation of its resolved CO (2-1) disk.

evidence.quote: Accurate mass measurement is therefore key to distinguishing the planet-mass scenario from the stellar-mass scenario.
This Letter makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.00773.S.
FW Tau was observed with ALMA Band 6 during Cycle 3, on 2016 September 14.

The data were reduced using the ALMA pipeline in the `CASA` package.
J0510+1800 was used as the bandpass and flux calibrator, and J0433+2905 was used as the the gain calibrator.

self_calibration.value: One iteration of phase-only self-cal on 2 GHz continuum basebands; not possible for CO baseband

evidence.quote: We employed one iteration of phase-only self-calibration to the 2 GHz continuum basebands.
We then CLEANed the calibrated data using the multi-frequency synthesis mode and natural weighting to enhance sensitivity in the images.
The CO channel maps (top panel of Figure [3](#fig:channel_maps)) have a beam size of $0.30\ensuremath{''}\times0.16\ensuremath{''}$ with a PA of $160.3\ensuremath{^\circ}$

final_rms.value: continuum 35 uJy/beam; CO 4.5 mJy/beam in signal-free channels

evidence.quote: a mean rms of 4.5 mJy beam$^{-1}$ in signal-free channels

what.value: Keplerian disk modeling procedure (radiative transfer channel-map fitting) follows earlier work, with own codes

evidence.quote: we follow the modeling procedure described in (cite: Cz15) to fit our channel maps with synthetic channel maps produced from radiative transfer models.
Here, we assume a conservative distance uncertainty of 20 pc following (cite: Cz16).

method.value: ALMA pipeline in CASA, phase-only self-cal on continuum, CLEAN with MFS and natural weighting

evidence.quote: We then CLEANed the calibrated data using the multi-frequency synthesis mode and natural weighting to enhance sensitivity in the images.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit continuum geometry and dust mass

method.value: Uniform-brightness inclined disk fit to continuum visibilities with MCMC; dust mass from optically thin formula

evidence.quote: We fit the model directly to the continuum visibilities using the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) package `emcee`

assumptions.value: T = 20 K, kappa = 2.3 cm^2/g, distance 140 pc, optically thin

evidence.quote: We use standard assumptions of $T = 20$ K and $\kappa_{\nu} = 2.3$ cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ and a distance to FW Tau C of 140 pc.
We fit the model directly to the continuum visibilities using the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) package `emcee`

analysis_steps.goal: Fit Keplerian CO disk model for stellar mass

method.value: RADMC-3D synthetic 12CO(2-1) channel maps, Fourier transformed and fit to visibilities with emcee

evidence.quote: Those synthetic channel maps are Fourier transformed and fit directly to the visibilities using the MCMC fitting package `emcee` (cite: FM13), with uniform priors for all parameters.

key_parameters.value: Free: Mdisk, Rdisk, gamma, T0, q, xi, M*, vsys, inclination, PA, small centering offset

evidence.quote: the density, temperature, and velocity structure of the system are described by the following parameters: $M_{\rm disk}$, $R_{\rm disk}$, $\gamma$, $T_0$, $q$, $\xi$, $M_*$, and $v_{\rm sys}$.

assumptions.value: Flared LTE vertically isothermal Keplerian disk; X_CO=1e-4; mu=2.37; inner radius 0.1 au; distance 140 pc with 20 pc uncertainty added in quadrature

evidence.quote: Here, $X_{\rm CO} = 1 \times 10^{-4}$ is the CO mass abundance fraction, and $\mu = 2.37$ is the mean molecular weight.

fitting.value: emcee, uniform priors, 128 CPUs, few days

evidence.quote: we run the fit over 128 CPUs on the University of Arizona El Gato supercomputer, and the modeling took a few days to converge.

validation.value: Convergence when walkers reached steady state; PV diagram compared with 10 Mjup and 0.1 Msun Keplerian curves

evidence.quote: The models were determined to be converged when the `emcee` walkers had reached a steady state with measured best-fit values changing minimally over a large number of steps.

used_for.value: ALMA pipeline reduction, self-calibration, CLEAN imaging

evidence.quote: The data were reduced using the ALMA pipeline in the `CASA` package.

used_for.value: MCMC fitting of continuum and CO visibilities

evidence.quote: Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) package `emcee` (cite: FM13)

used_for.value: Synthetic 12CO(2-1) channel maps from disk models

evidence.quote: We use the 3D radiative transfer modeling package `RADMC-3D` (cite: Dullemond12) to calculate the level populations in each cell

results_numeric.quantity: Stellar (dynamical) mass of FW Tau C

evidence.quote: it has a 1.3 mm flux of $\sim$2.06 mJy

results_numeric.quantity: FW Tau AB dust mass 3sigma upper limit

evidence.quote: the $3\sigma$ upper limit for a unresolved source suggests a dust mass $\lesssim$0.07 $M_\oplus$

findings_qualitative.value: FW Tau C gas disk is resolved and Keplerian; FW Tau AB undetected

evidence.quote: its dust disk is compact and likely unresolved; in contrast, the gas disk is more extended and clearly shows a Keplerian rotation.

claims.hypothesis: FW Tau C is a ~10 Mjup planet
claims.experiment: Keplerian modeling of resolved 12CO(2-1) disk and PV diagram
claims.result: M* = 0.098±0.015 Msun; velocity profile incompatible with 10 Mjup
claims.finding: FW Tau C is a low-mass star with an inclined disk; FW Tau is a triple of ~0.1 Msun stars

evidence.quote: It is clear that the velocity profile of the FW Tau C disk is incompatible with the 10 $M_{\rm Jup}$ rotation curve

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: 10 Mjup planetary-mass scenario rejected in favor of low-mass star embedded in an inclined disk

evidence.quote: Hence, FW Tau C is not a planetary-mass object, but is rather a low-mass star with an inclined disk

limitations_admitted.value: Single optically thick CO line likely underestimates gas mass

evidence.quote: with a single optically thick CO line, we are very likely to underestimate the true gas mass by a factor of few or even orders of magnitude

referee_caveats_inferred: Mass depends linearly on assumed 140 pc distance
